analysis.title: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT): 1QFY Preview & Maia 300 updates
key_insights: GS rates MSFT Buy (Conviction List) with a 12-month price target of $640 versus a $539.44 price (18.6% upside). The target is unchanged and based on 28x P/E on SNTM adjusted net income. The stock is up 38% since 4Q EPS on 7/29 versus the Nasdaq up 10%.

MSFT reports 1QFY (September) results on 10/28. GS sees a reasonable upside case of Azure growth of 46-47% cc versus 44-45% cc guidance and the Street at 45% cc, and 2QFY guidance of about 46-47% cc versus the Street at 45% cc.

Microsoft has already incorporated the drivers of the 3% 4QFY Azure beat into its 1QFY guide: 4Q infrastructure optimization (better dock-to-live times, fleet utilization) and GitHub's move to consumption-based pricing.

GS estimates Microsoft can bring about 5GW of capacity online in FY27 versus about 4GW in FY26, arriving unevenly. Directing compute to first-party apps (Copilot) and internal R&D (MAI) trades off Azure growth, and GS thinks the allocation mix is close to steady state.

From the CFO fireside chat on 9/9 and IR meetings on 9/15-16: Microsoft controls more variables in its capex equation than six months ago, because short-dated capex and CPUs are a bigger share of spend. GS thinks Microsoft may provide more ROIC datapoints soon, and that the Copilot apps strategy is working.

Investor concerns this week: (1) credit market volatility making data center financing costlier, and (2) the debate over token demand and monetization at the frontier versus off the frontier. GS says Microsoft's cost of capital should stay well below pure-play neoclouds and in line with investment-grade peers, and that the bigger opportunity is a model-agnostic enterprise harness.

GS sees M365 Commercial Cloud growth of 17-18% cc in 1QFY versus 17% cc guidance, driven by Copilot penetration, E7 adoption and consumption workloads. FY27 is the first year Microsoft has guided to M365 Commercial Cloud acceleration in recent history.

GS expects E7 adoption to outpace E5 after general availability in May, helped by Agent 365 (flat seat-based pricing for agentic governance). The monetization opportunity is moving from seats toward units of work, and the consumption opportunity may eventually exceed per-user revenue.

Margin worry on Copilot (seat-based pricing against rising usage) is eased by guidance for stable Cloud gross margins in F1Q. Microsoft has levers (fair usage limits, premium AI capabilities, usage-based pricing), and in a capacity-constrained setting can steer compute to Copilot, likely the higher-margin route, rather than Azure.

GS thinks upward revisions to FY27 Street capex may be limited. The Street expects about $221bn of FY27 capex (+52% y/y after +65% in FY26), and Microsoft has guided to about $175bn of CY26 capex, so 1HFY27 is already in the guide. The Street assumes a further 11% half-on-half step-up in 2HFY27.

Capex mix has shifted: long-dated assets fell from about 50% to about 33% of total capex over three quarters, and CPUs now exceed GPUs within short-dated capex. The constraint is space to deploy, not chips. Less constrained capex gives Microsoft more room to adjust to demand.

Microsoft's infrastructure strategy targets a broad set of enterprise workloads rather than frontier model development. Evidence cited: stepping back from parts of Stargate capacity, and all of the $51bn 4Q RPO increase coming from non-frontier customers.

GS argues the ROIC debate now matters more than the capex debate, and expects Microsoft may disclose more on AI returns, as Google and CoreWeave have done with GPU payback periods. GS sees no structural reason AI margins cannot approach cloud margins.

GS estimates revenue per GW rising from about $12bn in FY26 to about $13bn in FY30, and scale to about 40 GW of capacity by mid-2030. Levers for upside: Copilot monetization, inference intensity, software-layer monetization, platform attach, pricing and silicon efficiency.

On 10/12 Microsoft announced Maia 300, its third-generation custom inference accelerator, with deployment starting in 2027. The goal is for Maia to become the primary inference system across Microsoft products, alongside ramping AMD volumes as a second merchant GPU supplier to Nvidia.

Maia 200 is in production, deployed in the US, Europe and Australia, serving Copilot and MAI model development, with GitHub Copilot and Foundry to follow by year end. Microsoft says it delivers up to 1.7x more tokens per watt than leading GPU infrastructure.

Maia 300 claims: 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, up to 7x rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200 in a 96-accelerator configuration, 2.5x HBM bandwidth, 33% more memory capacity, over 2.5x performance per watt, 288 GB HBM4 and 18 TB/s per accelerator, built on TSMC N2P.

Maia software stack readiness is unproven at production scale, and industry feedback says Microsoft has more work to do. GS still sees Maia as a positive for bringing Azure AI compute gross margins closer to CPU-based workloads.

GS cut FY27E EPS to $19.21 from $19.38 and raised FY28E to $23.08 from $22.97 and FY29E to $27.87 from $28.05, reflecting Microsoft's updated segment reporting. Revenue is $389/$472/$570bn for FY27/28/29E versus $390/$471/$569bn before.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and Conviction List. GS calls MSFT the best-positioned name in its software coverage to benefit from compounding AI product cycles, with Azure, Copilot and Maia as levers.

sector_views.rationale: MSFT is named best positioned in GS Americas Software coverage to benefit from compounding AI product cycles.

earnings_insights: MSFT 1QFY (September quarter) results are due 10/28/2026. GS upside case: Azure growth of 46-47% cc versus company guidance of 44-45% cc and Street consensus of about 45% cc.
GS sees 2QFY27 Azure guidance of about 46-47% cc versus Street at 45% cc.
GS sees M365 Commercial Cloud growth of 17-18% cc in 1QFY versus company guidance of 17% cc.

GS EPS estimates (diluted, pre-exceptionals): FY27E $19.21 (old $19.38), FY28E $23.08 (old $22.97), FY29E $27.87 (old $28.05). FY26 actual $17.28. Quarterly GS EPS: 9/26E $4.71, 12/26E $4.65, 3/27E $4.79.
GS FY27E/FY28E/FY29E revenue $389.4bn/$471.9bn/$570.1bn versus FY26 actual $331.8bn. Street FY27 capex is about $221bn per Visible Alpha consensus, versus GS FY27E capex of $191.0bn.
The 4QFY (reported 7/29) Azure beat was 3%, and $51bn of RPO increase came entirely from non-frontier customers.

trade_ideas.description: Long MSFT (Buy, Conviction List) into 1QFY earnings on 10/28 with a 12-month price target of $640
trade_ideas.rationale: Azure and M365 Commercial Cloud acceleration, Copilot monetization and Maia silicon improving unit economics.
trade_ideas.risk: Longer ramp for internal silicon, spending outside expectations, leadership changes, and a shift to custom software that hurts the applications business.

risk_factors: Longer ramp for internal silicon could limit market share gains or gross margin expansion.
Greater investments in projects outside expectations (for example non-Azure).
A more meaningful shift to custom software could hurt the applications business.
Credit market volatility could make data center builds more expensive and harder to finance.
Maia software compatibility and performance are unproven at production scale.
Upward capex revisions without matching Azure revenue revisions have weighed on the stock in prior quarters.

tension_points.bull_case: Microsoft controls more capex variables, so Street FY27 capex revisions may be limited. Azure is supply constrained, Copilot monetization is improving, and AI margins could approach cloud margins.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex revisions without matching Azure revenue upside have weighed on the stock before, and GS's own revenue per GW is only about flat from $12bn to $13bn through FY30. Credit volatility could raise financing costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upward FY27 capex revisions without commensurate Azure revenue revisions, as in prior quarters.

theme_stances.key_argument: Azure acceleration through FY27 could be achievable from capacity coming online, utilization, software optimization, infrastructure efficiency and monetization.
theme_stances.evidence: Azure acceleration through FY27 could be achievable

theme_stances.key_argument: Maia 200 and Maia 300 should bring Azure AI compute gross margins closer to CPU-based workloads over time.
The ROIC debate matters more than the capex debate, and Microsoft's integrated stack should support stronger unit economics.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe the ROIC debate matters more than the capex debate.
